analysis: The sole change replaces the reservation cap with the larger operand. The unchanged caller subtracts this result directly from stock. For requested > stock, the new result is negative; for requested < stock, it removes all stock despite a smaller request. Equal operands remain correct, but that case does not establish correctness across the contracted domain. Both failures arise from the same changed operator and were absent at base.
coverage: Read every snapshot input, including contract, diff, review provenance and generic discovery/challenge/verification material. Inspected the pinned head file inventory and both change.mjs and caller.mjs at base and head. The two-file repository contains one affected caller. Release was excluded as requested.
limitations: Source reasoning only; no project code or executable checks were run, as instructed.

findings.claim: Math.max causes reserve to overdraw stock when demand exceeds stock and to over-fulfill smaller requests.
findings.evidence: At head, allowed(requested, available) returns Math.max(requested, available), and caller.mjs:2 returns stock - allowed(requested, stock). Thus reserve(3, 5) evaluates to -2, violating the nonnegative-stock invariant; reserve(5, 2) evaluates to 0 rather than 3, consuming three extra units. At base, Math.min produces 0 and 3 respectively. Restore the cap so the reserved quantity is min(requested, stock).
